headline: Highest risk is medium: shared workspace and vendor-backed ingestion create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascade paths; no direct evidence of a dangerous default bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can ingest workspace pages and databases, and its workspace state is shared across instances; the other agent is a prompt-leakage corpus with no runtime protections shown. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content in shared pages influences downstream interpretation. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_b-derived content is copied into a shared Notion page or database
IF agent_a is asked to summarize or act on that page without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict shared pages to trusted editors only
Add a provenance banner to imported content
Separate attacker-facing notes from operational workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content and sends data to vendor backends; agent B is a prompt-leakage repository with no stated data controls. If sensitive workspace material is placed into the shared workspace, A can transmit it to third-party model providers. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are stored in the shared workspace
IF agent_a processes those documents and forwards them to vendor backends
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Limit Notion pages to non-sensitive summaries
requires-engineering: enforce data-class labeling and routing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation, while agent B has no write or network capability listed. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because the relevant write surfaces are absent in both profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF hidden capabilities exist beyond the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared workflows
Avoid granting shared git or filesystem writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so its outputs can be treated as authoritative summaries. The other agent is a prompt-leak corpus that can seed misleading content. If B-derived text is inserted into A's workspace, A may propagate errors without verification. This is an inferred interaction, not directly observed.
conditions: IF B-generated text is added to pages that A summarizes
IF downstream users act on A's summary without independent verification
mitigations: Limit A to drafting, not decision support

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A is vendor-hosted and processes workspace content through Notion-controlled backends, while agent B has no data classes or residency commitments listed. The main compliance issue is that sensitive workspace data could leave the local environment when A is used; B does not add a documented residency mismatch. Because only A has a clear compliance surface, one citation is sufficient.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Notion workspace
IF organizational policy forbids vendor-hosted processing for that data class
mitigations: Review vendor DPA and retention settings
Use redacted copies for AI tasks
requires-engineering: route regulated data to approved systems
